_readme: CLEAR-BUG REGISTRY. A bug the owner reported, or one confirmed from stored evidence, goes here the moment it is confirmed - and the pre-push gate (scripts/admin/check-open-bugs.js) BLOCKS every push while any entry is open. That is the point: a reported bug is fixed immediately, not backlogged. Only CLEAR bugs belong here (reproduced, or owner-reported with evidence); design questions and improvements go to the task list instead. Close an entry by setting status to 'fixed' with the commit hash IN THE SAME COMMIT as the fix. Emergency escape: PUSH_WITH_OPEN_BUGS=1 git push (documented, visible, deliberate).

bugs.title: The trial front cover was an edit of the RAW landmark photograph (a Wikimedia close-up of a silhouette artist and his customer) - two strange men were painted beside the child
bugs.source: Owner-reported, production trial story job_1790169018278_n57xpnufo (6 pages, LOC001 "Parvis Notre-Dame - Place Jean-Paul II" on every page). Read back from stories.data: coverImages.frontCover has modelId grok-imagine-image-2.0, landmarkPhotos = [Parvis Notre-Dame variant 2], NO emptySceneImage, and its packed slot 0 (debug/frontCover/v0/grok-ref-0.jpg) is the raw 800x450 photograph of a bearded man having his silhouette cut by an older man. Every page's slot 0 (e.g. p1 grok-ref-0) is instead the painted, people-free plate of the cathedral square (vantage LOC001.1).
bugs.rootCause: storyJobPipeline.js onCoverScene (trial front cover) resolved the landmark with getLandmarkPhotosForScene and handed it straight to generateImageOnly as landmarkPhotos with no sceneBackground. packReferences (grok.js) promotes landmarkPhotos[0] to the scene-anchor slot whenever no plate is supplied, so the cover was an edit of the photograph - people and all. Trial pages turn that photo into a people-free plate first and send only the plate; the full-account cover plates it inside buildCoverReferences. The trial cover was the one path that never did.
bugs.impact: Every trial whose cover location is a real landmark shipped a cover rendered on top of a real photograph: strangers from the photo copied into the book's marketing image, photographic framing instead of the book's art style.
bugs.fix: The trial cover calls buildCoverReferences (shared with every full-account cover) with sceneBackground = the plate the trial pages rendered for the cover LOC (trialPlatesByLoc) and requirePlate: true; with no page plate the helper renders a cover plate from the setting only, and a landmark with no plate throws. The raw-photo path and hand-rolled VB grid are deleted. Pinned by tests/unit/trial-cover-plate-not-raw-photo.test.ts; replayed over the stored story (slot 0 = page plate, photo not packed) plus one $0.04 render.

bugs.title: On two trial pages the built image prompt carried no scene description and no character reference list at all - the illustrator was never told what the page was
bugs.source: Production trial story job_1789975900382_dyc1g7wue ("Noam et le Pont des Brindilles", fr-ch, 6 pages, watercolor, 2026-09-21 05:31 CH). Read back from story_jobs.result_data. Pages 1,2,3,6 carry the full block in sceneImages[].prompt (imageSummary prose + "Setting:" + "Camera:" + "Depth:" + AGE & PROPORTIONS, WORN ITEMS and the character reference list). Pages 4 and 5 carry NONE of them: the p5 prompt (6,525 chars) contains zero occurrences of "Leo", "ravine", "tower", "far side" or "entrance", and its first character-name mention is at offset 6,095 inside the EXACT POSES tail. What survives on both pages is REQUIRED OBJECTS, SEASON, ART STYLE, the rule blocks, EXACT POSES and EXPRESSIONS - i.e. everything fed by extractSceneMetadata, and nothing fed by stripSceneMetadata or referencePhotos. The rendered images corroborate the prompts rather than merely logging them: p5 omits Leo entirely (the brief places him at the tower entrance) and depicts the wrong moment (standing, pulling the rope) instead of the declared crossing.
bugs.rootCause: CONFIRMED - the prompt SHRINK, not the trial path. sceneImages[].prompt stores what was SENT (genResult.prompt, storyJobPipeline.js:1391), not what was built, and both of these pages were fitted to the Grok-edit body budget by shrinkPromptForModel -> sectionAwareCut (server/lib/images.js). The cut of the day found a droppable block EXTENT by scanning forward to the next header in a hand-kept CUT_BLOCK_MARKERS list; a page whose headers after AGE & PROPORTIONS were not in that list (no REFERENCE CARD COLOURS, no THIS IMAGE DEPICTS) had the scan run to the end of the head, so one named drop deleted AGE & PROPORTIONS, WORN ITEMS, the scene prose, the per-character lines, Setting/Camera/Depth and the character reference list together. Reproduced from the stored p5 brief: replaying the real buildImagePrompt over it (8,913 chars) and running the historical cut against the page budget returns exactly the two opening rule paragraphs plus the tail - byte-for-byte the shape stored in production, AGE/WORN/Setting/Leo all absent. Not trial-specific: both the trial page render and the full/unified page render call the one shrinkPromptForModel; the trial path is merely the exposed one, because Grok EDIT fits the body to the model cap MINUS the edit prefix. The earlier no-shrink reading came from generationLog: recordPromptShrink did not exist when this story ran, so a shrink could leave no generation event at all.
bugs.impact: Any trial page can be rendered with no scene description and no cast block while still looking like a complete prompt. Trial runs skip quality eval and repair by design, so nothing downstream catches it: this story shipped to a real user with its climax unillustrated and a named friend missing from the page that introduces him. Hit 2 of 6 pages (33%) on this run. The full path is the sibling to check - it passes scene.sceneDescription, not page.sceneHint.
bugs.fix: Root cause removed by 865f983f7 (sectionAwareCut rewritten to remove each droppable block by its EXACT text read from prompts/image-generation.txt, with page facts ranked to go LAST, and the shrink recorded as a generation event). Made unreintroducible by FIXCOMMIT: sectionAwareCut now measures what each drop is entitled to remove (blockExtent) and THROWS if a drop reaches past its own block - a prompt that does not state the page is the wrong picture, not a cheaper one. Behaviour pinned by tests/unit/prompt-cut-protects-the-page.test.ts (6 tests): an over-cap page keeps its scene prose, cast, AGE & PROPORTIONS and WORN ITEMS at both the page and the Grok-edit budget, the head never collapses to the opening rules, and a drop is confined to the block it names.

bugs.title: crowdExpected was declared only in the fallback Art Director template, so the crowd guard read false on every page and correct crowds took extra_character CRITICALs
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789420511893_zly5rcdej (generated 2026-09-14 23:15 -> 2026-09-15 00:38 CH). Stored sceneMetadata has crowdExpected=false on all 16 pages while 11 of the 16 briefs contain crowd/onlooker/quay/Hafen wording; 9 pages took an extra_character CRITICAL for harbour crowds the brief asked for and the renderer drew correctly (p1: 12 figures for a cast of 3; p2: 10/3; p4: 10/1; p8: 10/1). Mean finalScore 43 against 62-69 on the three preceding stories, which carried 0-1 extra_character findings each. The guard is correct end to end - sceneMetadata.js:883/921/1082 reads metadata.crowdExpected === true, evalPipeline.js:1087 carries it into the cast roster, evalPipeline.js:1452 declines the finding - but the field was declared ONLY in prompts/scene-expansion.txt, the per-page FALLBACK template. The live beats path expands with prompts/scene-expansion-all.txt (beatsPipeline.js:1715 fallback log proves it), which discusses crowds in five places but had no crowdExpected key in its metadata schema and no rule; an omitted key reads as false. Compounding: extra_character keeps CRITICAL (scoring.js ~186), its inpaint route was closed 2026-09-13 (NOT_INPAINTABLE_TYPES, repairLogic.js ~980, commit 0f25e7f25) and selectCharRepairTasks (repairLogic.js:444) keys on a cast name a surplus figure does not have, so wasCharacterFixed=false on all 16 pages - the false CRITICALs could only subtract.
bugs.fix: prompts/scene-expansion-all.txt declares "crowdExpected": false in its metadata schema and carries the rule, mirroring prompts/scene-expansion.txt:175 verbatim and generically. Pinned by tests/unit/scene-expansion-template-parity.test.ts, which asserts the two Art Director templates declare the SAME metadata key set - so the next field added to one reaches the other. Verified against the stored briefs of job_1789420511893_zly5rcdej; no regeneration and no paid call. See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-15 "crowdExpected must be declared by BOTH Art Director templates" and tasks/staging-story-review-2026-09-15.md.

bugs.title: On a grid mismatch a detected cell that merged several drawn panels was cropped and stored as ONE element's reference image
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi, stored generationLog: three vb_sheet_layout_mismatch events in one run ('drew 9 cells (3x3) for 3 requested', 'drew 2 cells (2x1) for 3 requested', 'drew 6 cells (3x2) for 2 requested') plus vb_sheet_element_missing for the boulder entry. On the 2x1 sheet the gutter detector merged three stacked panels into one cell; identifySheetCells named that cell for a single element and splitGridIntoReferences cropped and stored it, so that entry's reference image shows a signpost, a cave wall and a boulder at once. Every downstream prompt fed that reference is shown three objects and told they are one.
bugs.fix: splitGridIntoReferences now measures each MAPPED crop with detectSheetGrid (countPanelsPerCell, no model call) and rejectMultiPanelAssignments (server/lib/sheetGrid.js, pure) drops any assignment whose cell re-detects as more than one panel: that element gets NO reference (logged as vb_sheet_cell_multi_element) instead of a multi-object one. Detection failure counts as one panel, so the check can never invent a drop, and the run continues either way. Tests: tests/unit/reference-sheet-mismatch.test.ts.

bugs.title: A reference cell re-rendered after a failed gate was given the identical prompt, so it reproduced the same failure
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi: vb_state_cells_rerender then vb_state_cells_still_bad with a WORD-FOR-WORD identical reason, twice ('The left wing membrane is ragged in the first image and smooth in the second image...' for one entry, 'The color of the object in the second image is a darker, more muted teal...' for another). rerenderSolo called buildReferenceSheetPrompt with exactly the arguments of the first render; the judge's reason was logged and discarded.
bugs.fix: buildReferenceSheetPrompt takes an optional gateReason and appends the judge's own sentence as a PREVIOUS ATTEMPT REJECTED note (quoted, never interpreted in code; sanitised with the rest of the prompt). rerenderSolo passes it on both paths - element/character cell and state-cell batch. The fail-open 'accepted anyway' behaviour is unchanged; that is an open owner decision.

bugs.title: A size comparison in a bible description is rendered as cast members in the element cell
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi: both state cells of the creature entry render four children and a dog sitting on its back, because its description says 'large enough for four small children and a dog to sit across the back between the wing roots and the base of the neck'. Same class as the production ART001 prop described as 'roughly the size of two open palms', which rendered two human hands on it (tasks/BACKLOG.md). prompts/reference-sheet.txt carried the rule only under FOR OBJECTS/ARTIFACTS, and only for a 'comparison'; a creature entry never reaches that section.
bugs.fix: A global REQUIREMENTS line in prompts/reference-sheet.txt: 'Only the element itself is drawn. A person, animal or object the description names to convey its size or scale is never drawn' - so it binds every cell, not just the objects section. The bible prompt is untouched (owned by another session). Test: tests/unit/reference-sheet-mismatch.test.ts.

bugs.title: firstQuoted() closed a lector finding's quoted span on the NEXT apostrophe, truncating any span containing one and silently discarding the finding
bugs.source: Reproduced from stored evidence on staging story job_1788681313413_xqmtk2gcs. parseLectorFindings (server/lib/textRefine.js) read each side of 'PAGE n: <quote> -> <correction>' with firstQuoted(), which took the text between the opening quote character and the NEXT one. On "'the boy's pole lantern went dark like the rest.'" the closing quote was read as the apostrophe inside boy's, so quote became 'the boy' and correction likewise truncated; the quote===correction guard then dropped the whole finding at the PARSE step, before locate ever ran. A second finding, 'everyone's' -> 'everyone else's', hit the same trap and applied correctly only because its two truncations happened to differ. Every possessive and every contraction in English, and every apostrophe in French, was affected.
bugs.note: Fixed by reading first-to-LAST quote character per side (quotedSpan), after stripping a trailing parenthetical alternative; an unbalanced quote now rejects the line instead of half-parsing it. Unit tests: tests/unit/lector-quote-parse.test.ts.

bugs.title: calculateTextCost returns $0 for google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview: MODEL_PRICING has no entry and no fallback match reaches it
bugs.source: Reproduced from server/config/models.js: MODEL_PRICING (~lines 999-1053) has no key for 'google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview' and none of calculateTextCost's three fallbacks (models.js:1091-1095) match it, so it hits the '[COST] No token pricing found' warn branch and returns 0. bugs.note: MODEL_PRICING entry added with prices read from OpenRouter's public catalogue (GET /api/v1/models, 2026-09-06): $2.00 input / $12.00 output per 1M tokens, thinking = output (reasoning bills at the completion rate and is already inside completion_tokens). Reconciled exactly against the measurement: 2404 in / 21387 out predicts $0.2615 vs direct_cost $0.2615. direct_cost remains authoritative; this is the fallback. The >200k-prompt long-context tier ($4/$18) is not modelled - documented in the code comment. See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-06.

bugs.title: 60-min total-age cap in the status poll (and the create-path 120-min 'abandoned' branch) kills healthy long runs; heartbeat defeated by paid-call loops had no spend backstop
bugs.source: dragonrun1 staging run job_1788551692337_bc479p945: killed at 89% by a status poll at job age 64 min ('Job timed out after 64 minutes') while the pipeline was healthily in best-version selection; pipeline kept running in the background (progress advanced to 94% after the flip), story saved, completion UPDATE blocked by the WHERE status='processing' guard
bugs.note: Owner ruling 2026-09-04: heartbeat staleness (10 min) is the sole stall detector; total age becomes a 180-min runaway backstop (server/routes/jobs.js, both kill sites incl. the age-only 'abandoned' branch that fired regardless of a fresh heartbeat). Added JOB_SPEND_CAP_USD=15 (~3x a normal $4.93 run) in storyJobPipeline.js: live cost accumulates in addUsage (exact direct_cost for Grok/Runware, MODEL_PRICING for token providers, per-image fallback) and trips at the next checkCancellation checkpoint, failing the job loudly — covers paid-call loops that keep the heartbeat fresh.

bugs.title: Failed eval becomes evaluated:true / finalScore 100 and beats every real repair in pick-best
bugs.source: fault-hunt agent A (silent-default class), verified against images.js batch wrapper + scoring.js applyScore + repairPipeline null tripwire; same disease as the 2026-08-24 dead evaluator, one seam higher

bugs.title: Edit-mode body character repair produces nothing: the spine gate battery rejects every draw because Grok always re-renders the scene in box mode
bugs.source: owner: 'we already fixed this before and it was working' — G7, job_1788215224103_avu132n7je p16 (Lorena). Stored retryHistory: 12/12 draws rejected across 4 endpoint calls (11x 'Model redrew the SCENE... background still differs by 27-71 grey levels' at samBlend.js bg-residual reject, 1x mask IoU 54%), before AND after the template fix e7447ec81. Stored attemptFrames prove Grok re-renders the whole 1024x1024 scene on every box-mode draw (figures preserved but reflowed, target ~1.3-1.6x oversized) — inherent model behaviour the WORKING design (d68bd8815 fullScene + 2026-07-11 old-union-new feather composite) absorbed by compositing only the figure union onto the ORIGINAL scene, with no rejection path at all. The Stage-3 spine merge (24842d2bd) routed fullScene through the uncalibrated crop-space gate battery and the 2026-08-06 box-mode bg-residual hard reject (premised on the model editing in place) finished it: body repair structurally cannot pass wherever Grok reflows.
bugs.note: samUnionBlend: background residual above 26 grey levels is registration telemetry (mode bg-rerendered, no shift applied), never a throw — the composite ships only the figure union, so the shipped background is the original by construction. New figure registration for body blends aligns the new silhouette bbox onto the old (height-ratio scale clamped [0.6,1.45], feet-anchored dy, centre-aligned dx; same affine on candidate + mask; kept only when bbox IoU improves >0.05; pure math unit-tested in tests/unit/figure-registration.test.ts). Every quality gate is UNCHANGED and judges the registered candidate: mask IoU 0.55, style-match, white-card, coverage, sharpness, figure-integrity naturalness — a genuinely re-posed figure still rejects. Dead Stage-3/5 orphans removed in the same commit: character-repair-grok-fullscene.txt + character-repair-gemini.txt loaders, featherComposite plumbing (UI toggle consumed by nothing; the service layer never forwarded it), RepairWorkflowPanel blackout option. Supersedes the 2026-08-06 box-mode background-reject decision (docs/decisions.md 2026-09-01). Verified on p16 via the same API route the UI uses after staging deploy.

bugs.title: Edit-mode character repair in fullScene (box) mode always dies at the blend gate - the crosshatch prompt is the CUTOUT template, so the model repaints the figure oversized
bugs.source: owner: 'character repair from edit mode did not work' on staging job_1788215224103_avu132n7je p16 (Lorena). Reproduced via POST /repair-workflow/character-repair: 3/3 Grok draws rejected by the blend gate ('background still differs by 60-71 grey levels' x5, 'mask IoU 54%' x1 across the owner's run + the repro). attemptFrames show the model repainting Lorena ~1.6x larger than the hatched silhouette, covering sand/boat background - the gate refuses correctly; the DRAW is bad every time. Root cause: faceRepair.js buildPrompt uses characterRepairCutout for every crosshatch treatment. In box mode the model receives the FULL scene, but that template calls IMAGE 2 'THE CUTOUT TO EDIT - a scene region' and has no silhouette-size rule. The pre-spine fullScene branch used characterRepairInpaint ('The crosshatch traces the exact silhouette - match its shape, size, and pose. Do not paint outside the crosshatch.'); the Stage-3 refactor (24842d2bd, 2026-07-26) collapsed both region sources onto the cutout template and left characterRepairInpaint orphaned (loaded by prompts.js, zero consumers).
bugs.note: faceRepair.js buildPrompt now threads regionSource and picks characterRepairInpaint for crosshatch+box (full scene), keeping characterRepairCutout for the cutout region path. character-repair-inpaint.txt gains the {appearanceContext} placeholder the cutout template already carried (exp #360 identity facts), passed from the same fill. Verified deployed: staging /api/health at 7426a1d2, re-run confirmed the new template in use (prompt 4166 -> 3669 chars, scene wording + size rule). The template regression is fixed; p16 itself STILL fails - Grok redraws the entire scene in every mode on that busy 6-figure page (12/12 draws rejected across fullScene and cutout) and the blend gate correctly refuses. That residual is model behaviour, tracked as an open BACKLOG item (body repair on busy pages), not this bug.

bugs.title: getLanguageNameEnglish('de-ch') returns bare 'Swiss German', which a model reads as Schwyzerdütsch dialect instead of Swiss Standard German
bugs.source: arc-create call (arcflow A/B) titled an arc «Nebel uf em Zürisee» - Swiss German DIALECT, not the Swiss Standard German (Hochdeutsch, ss never ß) that de-ch books must be written in. Root cause confirmed in server/lib/languages.js:344's getLanguageNameEnglish, whose de-ch entry (line 48, pre-fix) was nameEnglish: 'Swiss German'. A prior fix note already existed at server/lib/promptBuilders.js:4077-4082 (buildOutlineReviewPrompt) citing this exact trap causing a full-book dialect rewrite ('S'Fescht', 'blybt stoh') and working around it there by always pairing LANGUAGE with the full LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION + LANGUAGE_NOTE - but getLanguageNameEnglish itself, and every OTHER call site that emits bare LANGUAGE without instruction/note (buildOutlineReviewPrompt's own review-only injection at line 3948, plus two dead fallback string builders), stayed unfixed at the root.
bugs.note: server/lib/languages.js: de-ch nameEnglish -> 'Swiss Standard German (ss, never ß - never dialect)' (also fixed the identical bare label in the unused getAvailableLanguages() UI list at the same file, same trap). This is the single source of truth consumed by all ~13 call sites across promptBuilders.js and storyJobPipeline.js, so every consumer is fixed by the one change - none did a string equality check against 'Swiss German' (grepped, none found), so no consumer needed adjusting. Consolidated the duplicate hand-typed map at promptBuilders.js:4903 (buildTextProofreadPrompt) into a call to getLanguageNameEnglish instead of a second, narrower hard-coded 'de-ch' -> string mapping, per the sibling-paths rule (one source of truth for a value that exists in more than one place). Grepped prompts/*.txt for bare 'Swiss German' emissions: only the story-scorecard-judge*.txt family says 'Swiss German uses ss' - left untouched, that describes the orthography RULE for judging existing text, not an instruction to WRITE in dialect, matching the existing LANGUAGE_NOTE convention. Did not touch prompts/feedback-consolidator.txt or tests/unit/inpaint-routing.test.ts (out of scope, pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes).

bugs.title: Shared vantage plates are built from Visual Bible prose only - the Art Director's per-page emptyScenePrompt is discarded, and three selection bugs pick the wrong ground, vantage and shot
bugs.source: audit of 32 pages across 2 stories (incl. staging job_1787959478282_bz19gm36h): 25/30 plates were PROMPT-WRONG. p5 is the worked example - objects[] is [LOC003 reef passage, VEH001, ART003], the AD's emptyScenePrompt says the ship's deck planks fill the centre with the boom across frame, page shot is 'medium'; the shipped plate prompt contained none of that and carried SHOT: wide.
bugs.note: Four mechanisms, all in the vantage-canvas path (storyJobPipeline.js Phase 5a-pre-vantage), which the per-page path at the same phase never had. (1) The plate prompt was assembled from the vantage/LOC prose and DROPPED pageData.emptyScenePrompt - fixed by the hybrid plate: the AD prose is appended as a FRAMING block that outranks the setting lines, taken from the first page a shared plate serves, and the SHOT line now comes from the page's own shot. (2) getPrimaryVantageForPage took the FIRST LOC in objects[] as the camera's ground - fixed with an ordered selection: a LOC whose vantage's pages[] names this page, then the LOC the AD's emptyScenePrompt names, then an explicit dotted reference, then first-listed. (3) The vantages[0] fallback ignored each vantage's own pages[] - now matched before falling back. (4) Locations without vantages got a synthetic plate hard-coded to shot 'wide', overriding the page's framing - now inherits the page's shot. Plus the VEHICLES block demanded the whole vessel rendered even when the camera stands on it (duplicate ships, ships inside caves, wheels on land) - it now asks for the visible part only with an explicit camera-aboard clause, and the plate call carries one reference family (landmark photo XOR VB element render) named by a REFERENCE line. Template contradiction resolved: scene-expansion(-all).txt forbade dotted vantage ids for invented LOCs while story-bible-from-beats.txt asks the bible to create vantages for them. Verified by rendering p5's merged plate prompt from stored data: FRAMING carries the deck-filling prose, SHOT is medium, REFERENCE line present. Empty-scene QC is still not wired on the vantage path (open, see docs/decisions.md).

bugs.title: The 'drop locations when an empty-scene plate exists' filter has never fired on any non-trial story - it reads sceneBackgrounds before Phase 5a-pre fills it
bugs.source: reproduced on staging job_1787959478282_bz19gm36h: 14/14 pages with a grid shipped their locations AND the ship as grid cards despite every one of those pages having a plate. Census replayed getElementReferenceImagesForPage against the stored visualBible and matched the stored grid images cell-for-cell (stable ~639px cell pitch: 1920=3 cells, 2560=4, 3191=5, 3831=6) - every page's stored grid equals the UNFILTERED selection.
bugs.note: storyJobPipeline.js had `if (sceneBackgrounds[pageNum]) elementReferences = filter(type !== 'location')` inside the pageData map that PRODUCES pageDataArray. sceneBackgrounds is populated by Phase 5a-pre-vantage and Phase 5a-pre, which both CONSUME that array - so the map is {} at that point on every non-trial story and the branch is unreachable. Fix separates selection from construction: the map now stores vbElementRefs/vbSecondaryLandmarks only, and a new Phase 5a-pre-grid pass (placed after the plates exist, before every pageData.visualBibleGrid reader) applies the filter and builds the buffer. Filter now matches buildPageCompositeRefs: a plate drops BOTH location and vehicle cells; plateless pages keep everything. Same commit caps selection at 4 (was 6) at both page-grid call sites. Verified statically on the real story: 3-6 cells with a location on every page -> 1-4 cells, zero locations, no vehicle on any plated page. Related: buildPageCompositeRefs calls itself the 'single source of truth' for these filters but production page generation never calls it (only iteratePageCore + Test Lab do) - the pipeline keeps an inline copy. Also NOT fixed here: that inline copy passes secondaryLandmarks into buildVisualBibleGrid, contradicting the 2026-08-18 'a landmark photo NEVER enters the grid' decision.

bugs.title: VB reference grid arrives at Grok as a tiny thumbnail row (50x83px cells) instead of owning slot 3 at full size
bugs.source: owner (staging job_1787959478282_bz19gm36h p5) + measured from the stored grokRefImages: slot 3 is 683x683 and the two VB cells in it measure 50x83px each (0.9% of the slot area), while 2 of the grid's 4 elements were dropped entirely
bugs.note: Two defects in packReferences (server/lib/grok.js). (1) The own-slot gate `rawVbElements.length === visualBibleGrid.rawElements.length` abandoned the own slot whenever the grid still held a location, so the whole VB set fell back to composeCharWithVbRow's bundled thumbnail row and slot 3 went unused - inverting the owner's 2026-08-15 slot table on every such page. bugs.title: Staging analyzer cannot load GroundingDINO since the ArcFace/TensorFlow image rebuild — every detection 503s
bugs.source: staging runtime log: 6x "[GDINO] Loading GroundingDINO..." each followed by "GroundingDINO unavailable:" with EMPTY error (OOM-kill signature); Lab exps #799/#800 blocked/failed on /detect-figures-text HTTP 503 ~40min after deploy of f1448757b

The ArcFace commits (b123a2088 opt-in warmup, 36129ad73 idle reaper) hint at known pressure. Owner: the other agent (ArcFace author) is running a smoke test and owns this. Blocks verification of the identity fixes (task #29 exp on p1 waiting). UPDATE bbd41215: new build deployed, SAME crash loop (exp #801 failed identically, 503s). The empty error comes from get_groundingdino() (photo_analyzer.py:1975) — from_pretrained throws an exception whose str() is empty; the handler at :2089 prints only {load_err}. IMMEDIATE DIAGNOSTIC: log repr(load_err) + traceback there. Suspects: (a) transformers import path now touching the TF-2.13/protobuf-3.20.3 corridor (transformers auto-detects installed TF), (b) OOM during weight load with TF resident, (c) missing pre-downloaded weights in the rebuilt image (Dockerfile pre-download step vs new layer). ROOT CAUSE FOUND: Dockerfile layer order — requirements.txt (TF 2.13) downgrades typing_extensions below torch/transformers floor; the DINO pre-fetch layer ran BEFORE the typing_extensions>=4.12 repair layer, failed, was swallowed by || WARN, and the image shipped WITHOUT DINO weights; every runtime load re-downloaded ~900MB and died with an empty-str exception. FIX: typing_extensions upgrade moved BEFORE the pre-fetch layer; loader 503 path now logs repr+traceback+cache-presence so an empty str can never blind us again. CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (diagnostics from 538d2f540): transformers>=4.44 re-resolved to 5.x in the ArcFace rebuild; transformers 5 requires torch>=2.5 and DISABLES our torch 2.1.2 (held there by the numpy==1.24.3 co-pin TF 2.13 needs) — every model class raised PyTorch-not-found. Fixed by pinning transformers<5 (a057d8017). The layer-order fix (typing_extensions before pre-fetch) stays as hardening.

TensorFlow's ~350MB on top of GroundingDINO's ~1.9GB exceeded the container, so DINO died on load with an empty error and crash-looped. Disabled, no TF is imported at all and the analyzer returns to its pre-change footprint. The idle reaper could not have saved it: it requires the whole SERVICE to be idle, which never happens during a Lab run or a story. Re-enabling needs ArcFace out of the shared analyzer process.

bugs.title: Two torch wheels were installed over each other, leaving 2.9 GB of unusable NVIDIA CUDA libraries in a CPU-only container and a non-deterministic Python tree
bugs.source: Observed live via railway ssh: dist-packages held BOTH torch-2.1.2.dist-info (PyPI CUDA wheel) and torch-2.14.0+cpu.dist-info (pytorch CPU index), with torch.__version__ reporting 2.1.2+cu121 over a 2.14 file layout. Cause: the Dockerfile CPU-index layer said a bare 'torch torchvision', so it took whatever was newest (2.14.0+cpu), and 'pip install -r requirements.txt' then resolved torch again against PyPI — where the numpy==1.24.3 co-pin forces 2.1.2 — installing that CUDA wheel on top. Collateral measured: nvidia 2.9 GB + triton 277 MB in a container with no GPU (torch.cuda.is_available() False), and a Python stack of 7.8 GB.
bugs.note: RETRACTION — this entry originally claimed the collision had silently broken GroundingDINO in production since late August. THAT WAS WRONG, corrected by the owner. Evidence against it: staging story_metrics carry sam_calls/dino_calls on every substantial story through 2026-09-02, and the production stories with no dino counters are all 6-page ~140s unified TRIAL runs (which skip figure detection) — every 18-page beats story has them, including one on 2026-08-25 sitting between trials. The 'cannot import name ExportOptions' error I reproduced in a fresh shell is a KNOWN first-import race already documented and retried at photo_analyzer.py:2130 (2026-08-23); inside the analyzer torch is already imported, so DINO and SAM were working throughout. FIX (still worth it on its own terms): pin torch==2.1.2+cpu / torchvision==0.16.2+cpu — 2.1.2 is the version the numpy co-pin already forced, so this makes the second resolution a no-op instead of an overwrite. Verified on staging: a single torch-2.1.2+cpu.dist-info, nvidia tree gone, python stack 7.8 GB -> 3.8 GB, transformers imports in a cold shell, and GroundingDinoForObjectDetection + ultralytics SAM both load from the baked cache. A build-time assertion (torch must end in +cpu) now fails the build if a second torch ever lands again.

bugs.title: First photo upload after an analyzer deploy returns 502: the idle reaper kills the face worker mid-startup, and ensure_worker hands out a live-but-unbound worker
bugs.source: Reproduced on production immediately after the analyzer split went live (master cadd4ee72). POST /api/photos/remove-bg with tests/fixtures/demo-photos/berger/Emma.jpg: attempt 1 -> 502 'face worker call failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' in 0.8s; attempts 2-4 -> 200 with an identical 171710-byte result in 34.2s / 6.2s / 4.7s. Staging (warm container, up since 2026-09-04) returned 200 for the same call, so it presents as prod-only but is a cold-container race in both. Prod analyzer log ab4fb1ca, all within 19:50:53Z: '[WORKERS] spawning face worker on :5001' / '[WORKERS] killing face worker (sessions=0, idle)' / '[WARMUP] face worker warm failed: face worker exited during startup'.
bugs.note: Two defects, both in worker-lifecycle bookkeeping in photo_analyzer.py. (A) /warmup returns immediately and calls ensure_worker() on a BACKGROUND thread, so the warmup request's own teardown fires _maybe_reap_workers() with sessions=0 and nothing in flight and terminates the worker it just asked for. kill_workers' expect_epoch guard only sees REQUESTS, so an off-request bring-up was invisible to it; only the first role in the warmup loop died, which is why torch survived and face did not. (B) ensure_worker returned early on _worker_alive(), which is only 'poll() is None' — a process that has started but not yet bound its port passes it, so the caller got a URL that answered Connection refused. That is the literal 502. Fix: a REFCOUNTED _bringing_up map (refcounted because /warmup's thread and a concurrent upload can await the same role, and the first to finish would otherwise drop the protection) that kill_workers refuses to kill through, with an explicit force=True kept for the two callers documented as overrides (/release-memory?force=true and session_reset at Node boot); and a live-but-unproven worker now falls through to the readiness poll instead of short-circuiting. Note this means warmup never worked at all in the split service — every warm spawn of the first role was killed seconds later. Regression test: tests/manual/test_worker_bringup_race.py (fake Popen + fake health probe, no ML loaded).

bugs.title: buildCrosshatchTreatment has no coverage gate: a non-null but fully transparent SAM silhouette erases the whole hatch, so the image sent to Grok carries no repaint mark at all
bugs.source: Staging job_1788681313413_xqmtk2gcs back cover, Rachel. The three stored attemptFrames[*].charRepairWhiteout frames are byte-identical (338,468 bytes) and, measured over raw pixels, contain 0.000% magenta (max magenta-ness 38, identical to the untouched page) and 0.000% white, with the target's face sharp and unblurred. The recovered crop rect (x384 y0 340x545, by normalised cross-correlation against the page) matches resolveRegion's cutout+PAD_FACTOR 0.4 geometry, i.e. treatment 'crosshatch' — which always composites magenta. Grok's three outputs are whole-scene redraws, the behaviour expected of a model told to 'repaint the area covered by the magenta crosshatch' on an image with no crosshatch.
bugs.note: buildFaceTreatmentMask (whiteout and blur) throws at cov < 40. buildCrosshatchTreatment computes the same cov and discarded it, and only handled sil === null ('rectangular hatch'), never sil non-null-but-empty. dest-in against a fully transparent mask erased the hatch and clipped the face blur to nothing, so treatedBuf came out pixel-identical to the untouched crop and the run was a silent no-op that still paid for the model call. Fix: honour gateCoverage in the crosshatch path and fall back to the RECTANGULAR hatch — the degraded behaviour the function already documents and accepts for a null silhouette — with a warn and hatchClipped:false in treatmentInfo. Second, independent cause of the same owner report as repair-style-guard-forces-illustration-on-photographic-stories.

bugs.title: buildCharRepairRequest fills faceOnly with null, and repairCharacterMismatch treats null as a deliberate override — so every face repair silently becomes a full-figure repair
bugs.source: Measured from what RAN, not what was asked: Lab exp #996 on staging job_1788681313413_xqmtk2gcs was launched with whiteoutTarget 'face' + repairMode 'blended' — the exact combination the production 'Figur reparieren' button sends for Gesicht + Auto — and the stored result records descriptor 'grok:box:blur:body'. legacyFlagsToAxes resolves that input to 'grok:cutout:blur:face'. Reproduced offline: buildCharRepairRequest({imageBackend:'grok',whiteoutTarget:'face',faceBbox,bodyBbox}).faceOnly === null; images.js used `if (options.faceOnly !== undefined)`, null passes it, so explicitAxes.faceOnly = !!null = false; the body box (height 0.884 > 0.85) then trips the degenerate-cutout->box geometry guard, giving exactly the observed grok:box:blur:body.
bugs.note: buildCharRepairRequest materialises EVERY canonical key, filling absent ones with null, so faceOnly:null rides on every request the button, the automatic pipeline and the Test Lab build. treatment and regionSource were spared only because their guards are truthiness tests and null is falsy; faceOnly is the one boolean axis and the one that broke. Net effect: face-only repair has been unreachable through the shared contract since it landed — a face repair repaints the whole figure. Fix: treat null as 'not set' (`!== undefined && !== null`). An explicit faceOnly:false is still honoured. Regression cases in tests/unit/repair-style-guard-medium.test.ts.

bugs.title: A Visual Bible object with declared states gets NO reference image on any page: since d473434ed dropped the base cell, its state cells are emitted with null elementIds, so getElementReferenceImagesForPage cannot match the object and the paid multi-state sheet is silently discarded — every page renders the object invented, and its per-page state deltas are never applied
bugs.source: Confirmed from stored evidence: staging trial job_1788763045123_z8so79ngb (Emma, 5, de, adventure/mothers-day), run 2026-09-07 08:36 CH on staging commit 74d06fef. stories.data.referenceSheetBatches[2] = elementIds [null,null,null] with elementNames ["hand-drawn greeting card with a pressed flower — intact/torn and wet/repaired (artifact)"], while sibling batches carry real ids (batch0 [CHR001,CHR002], batch1 [LOC002,ART002]). Consequence visible in the stored page prompts: p1/p2/p3 contain NO "The attached reference images include" line at all, and p4/p5/p6 name only "fresh-picked flowers" (ART002, which has an id) — ART001 the greeting card, present on 5 of 6 pages and the story's central object, is referenced on none. The generated 3-state sheet (ref_sheet_source/p2/v0.jpg) is correct and unused: red crayon hearts, yellow suns, dried yellow flower; torn; mended with yellow ribbon. Every interior render invents the card instead (pink cosmos, no hearts or suns); the front cover renders it correctly because coverComposite uses a different path. Also explains the ignored state delta on p3 ("flower missing" — flower still attached). Root cause flagged independently by the author of the preceding state-model work: getElementReferenceImagesForPage's base-render fallback assumed a base cell exists, an assumption d473434ed removed.
bugs.note: Two causes, one class. (1) normaliseObjectStates - which mints each state dotted id (ART001.2) and its empty cell fields - was only called from visualBible.parseVisualBible, which has NO callers; the live parse path (outlineParser/unified.js extractVisualBible) spread the raw JSON and left states[] id-less. That was harmless while expandElementStateCells also emitted a base cell carrying the parent id; d473434ed removed the base cell, so the object ONLY had id-less cells - the rendered sheet could not be written back and no page could resolve one. Fixed by normalising states on the live path. (2) The Art Director cites the BARE parent id on nearly every page (6/6 pages of this story wrote [ART001]), partly because the States line it is shown rendered as [undefined], so resolution keyed only on a dotted handle never fired - hence the ignored p3 delta. Fixed by objectStateForPage: resolution is now cited handle -> the state the bible declares for this page -> the default (first) state, for both the reference cell and the REQUIRED OBJECTS delta clause. d473434ed verdict (4 states, 4 cells, no base cell) is NOT reversed. Silent degradation made loud: no-usable-cell, id-less rendered cell and id-less state row all log.error; an undeclared page log.warns; a missing state cell substitutes a sibling cell rather than shipping none. Sibling paths swept onto elementRefCell: empty-scene plates, the page-lookup location loop, the cover prop image (coverIterate) and the inpaint missing-element artifact reference (images.js). Verified with no paid calls by replaying job_1788763045123_z8so79ngb through the current builders: all 6 pages now carry ART001, p3 resolves to the torn and wet cell and its prompt carries the flower-missing delta. Tests: tests/unit/vb-object-states.test.ts (49). See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-07.

bugs.title: The 2x4 avatar sheet evaluator scores a sheet containing three strangers and no cell grid at 10/10 on every axis, so no avatar-sheet corruption can ever be caught automatically
bugs.source: Confirmed from stored evidence: staging job_1788763045123_z8so79ngb, data.styledAvatarGeneration[0]. The run passed skipQualityEval and every skip branch minted a passing 10 - generateComposited2x4's two row loops (review = { valid: true, score: 10 }), its finalScore = skipReview ? 10 : ... plus the ?? 10 sub-score defaults, and runStyleTransferPass's best = { score: 10, verdict: null } (stored record: passes.pass2.attempts[0].stage 'no-eval-requested', finalVerdict null, pass1 verdict with heads/bodies/identityReport all null and every score 10). Fixed: a skipped eval now records score null, evaluated false, evalSkipped 'skipQualityEval'; sub-scores null instead of 10; best-of-N ranks an unscored attempt below any judged one; styledAvatars reports innerFinalScore/combinedScore null with evaluated:false and logs 'shipped UNSCORED'. valid stays true so the sheet still ships (fail-open, unchanged). bugs.title: The iterate/repair path re-derives the story's SEASON from the render date, so every iterated page rendered in autumn carries autumn foliage regardless of the story's stored season
bugs.source: Reproduced from stored evidence on two staging stories, both stored season:'summer' — job_1788816451791_25b31uqlp (dragon) and job_1788820396445_9erw6xc01 (pirate). All four iterate-round-* image versions across the two runs carried '**SEASON:** Autumn' in their rebuilt prompts; every first-pass version carried Summer. Visible result: the pirate p13 climax renders its almond tree in full autumn orange while p15 and p16 render the same tree green — an internal continuity contradiction inside one book. Cause: pipelineStoryData (storyJobPipeline.js, unified image phase) never carried `season` or `createdAt`, and server/lib/season.js resolveSeason() falls back to `inputData.createdAt || new Date()`. The fallback is by design for a missing season, but the field simply never reached the object, so the fallback fired on every iterate. season.js's own doc comment states the intended behaviour it could not deliver: 'never from now at render time — a repair run months later must resolve the same season the pages were drawn in.' Hits every iterated page of every story rendered Sep–Nov, and equivalently in any other season.

bugs.title: A Visual Bible object STATE delta contradicting the page's own plan-line instant rode the REQUIRED OBJECTS line and won over the instant; a brief's cited state was trusted over the bible's page table with no log line
bugs.source: Reproduced from stored evidence on staging story job_1788816451791_25b31uqlp. Page 11's plan line: 'Kiaan holds the small chip against the big scale resting in the dry stone trough, the broken edges fitting together'. The stored bible gave ART001 (chip) state .2 'resting in an open upturned palm, fully visible from above' for pages [6,11] and ART010 (scale) state .1 'lying flat and still inside the dry stone trough, no hands touching it' for pages [11-14]; no state existed for the instant the beat names. The p11 brief cited both, promptBuilders.buildImagePrompt appended each delta verbatim to the REQUIRED OBJECTS line (`state: objectStateFor(artifact, handle) || objectStateForPage(artifact, pageNumber)`, then `stateNote = ' - ' + trimStateClause(delta)`), nothing compared a delta to the page's interactions[], and the render obeyed the states across two attempts (chip held up in a palm, edges never met). Second defect, same path: p2's brief cited ART001.2 against a table declaring .1 for p2, and p12's cited ART010.2 (on the horns, pages 16-17) against a table declaring .1 - the cited handle was taken first at both the prompt and the reference-cell site, silently. Cause of the p11 table: story-bible-from-beats.txt asked for a delta per state but never said the delta is derived from THAT page's plan line, so the model filed p11 under a neighbouring page's untouched look.
bugs.note: FIX: (a) prompts/story-bible-from-beats.txt - a state's delta is read off THAT page's plan line; a page whose instant handles or joins the object never receives a resting look; each state carries a structured `held` flag. (b) visualBible.resolveObjectState is the ONE resolver for both the REQUIRED OBJECTS clause and the reference cell: a chosen state whose `held` disagrees with the brief's interactions[] (hands:true rows naming the object) is `contradicted` and buildImagePrompt drops its delta with a WARN naming page, state id and the authored delta. (c) When the cited handle and the bible's page table disagree, the page contact arbitrates; with no verdict the table wins; both cases WARN with both ids. Bibles without `held` (every stored story) never contradict. Limit, recorded honestly: the AD's interactions[] are character-to-object rows only, so 'two objects meeting' (p11's scale, which no row names) and 'open palm vs pressed' are not structurally detectable in code - for those the prompt-side derivation rule (a) is the fix.

bugs.title: The staging Qwen3-VL blind inventory never ran on a story job: processUnifiedStoryJob passed the resolved DEFAULT quality model as qualityModelOverride, and runVisualInventory lets any override beat runtime `inventoryModel`
bugs.source: Reproduced from stored evidence on staging stories job_1788816451791_25b31uqlp (18 pages, 26 evaluated versions) and job_1788820396445_9erw6xc01 (16 pages, 19 versions), both generated after commit d64cf25c9 went live. bugs.title: A VB entity NAMED in a cover scene description reached the image model with no definition and no reference image — the model painted a phantom figure for it

bugs.source: Measured on staging job_1788957347999_ijseol49a (Bimo, generated 2026-09-09, after the trim shipped): beatsReviewReport.vbAssignmentTrim = { stripped: [VEH002 from page 8, VEH002 from page 18], pagesOverBudgetBefore: 2, pagesOverBudgetAfter: 0 }, yet stored data.visualBible.vehicles[VEH002].appearsInPages = [8,18] and the outline text still lists "pages": [8, 18]; rankPageElements over the stored bible shows pages 8 and 18 at 4 elements each. Cause: beatsPipeline.js:1046 parsed its OWN copy (bibleParser.extractVisualBible()), trimmed it at :1087, and never rewrote the transcript; storyJobPipeline.js:2756 did a FRESH parser.extractVisualBible() over the outline and that object became streamingVisualBible, was passed to every stage and persisted. Consequence: the scene review's vb_element_overflow findings persisted (5/5 survived all ten reviews in Lab 1157/1179 and were read as 'the reviewer cannot fix them'), the Lab measured the untrimmed bible, and a resume re-inflated the pages. The invented-peer age clamp (applySecondaryAgeBand, beatsPipeline.js:1069) had the same loss.

Tests: tests/unit/vb-trim-persisted.test.ts. See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-11 'Visual Bible trim was never persisted'.

bugs.title: Character-cell render gate failed a correctly-rendered non-human secondary character for not having human skin, burning a paid re-render and shipping the original anyway

bugs.title: The bible-time plan-line trim (trimVbAssignments) emptied appearsInPages for six Visual Bible entries — the story’s central prop and the signpost carrying its plot-critical text among them — so no reference cell was rendered for any of them, while the final scene briefs asked for exactly those ids
bugs.source: Staging job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi. The Visual Bible is written at beats stage 3, the briefs at stage 4; trimVbAssignments (beatsPipeline.js:1156) decided page ownership by matching entry NAME tokens against the page PLAN LINE, which is prose and never cites ids. It stripped 19 (element,page) claims and left ART003 (central prop, a large scale), ART006 (signpost bearing the readable text), ART009, ART010, ART014 and ART016 at appearsInPages:[]. getElementsNeedingReferenceImages (visualBible.js:2314) skips an entry below the minimum page count, so those six got no reference cell and never reached a page prompt. Proof the trim was wrong: the FINAL briefs of the same job cite them by id - stored sceneImages p10 sceneMetadata.objects = ["LOC004","ART006"].
bugs.fix: Page assignment is no longer guessed at bible time. vbElementBudget.applyBriefUsage(visualBible, scenes) rebuilds every entry appearsInPages (and its states[]/vantages[] rows) from what the FINAL briefs cite - bare ids, dotted state/vantage handles crediting parent and row, and secondary characters/animals a page names by name via entryNamedByRow - and runs in generateStoryViaBeats once the briefs are final, before rawOutline is assembled and before the caller kicks off generateReferenceSheet; the result is written back through syncVisualBibleSection so storyJobPipeline, resume and the Lab read the same pages. The trimVbAssignments call and the now-dead vb_trim_lost assertion are removed. Trial keeps the early path (no briefs exist yet, applyBriefUsage no-ops). Replayed over the stored job: ART006 [] -> [10] and LOC005 [11] -> [9,11,17]; reference cells before {ART015} / after {ART006, ART015, LOC005}. Tests: tests/unit/vb-brief-usage.test.ts. See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-11 Visual Bible page assignment comes from the FINAL scene briefs.

bugs.title: A Visual Bible entry with states[] was only checked for consistency BETWEEN its states, never for depicting the object its description describes - so a lamp that rendered as a CCTV camera in both cells stored a PASS
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi. referenceSheets.js had two mutually exclusive gate branches: a state batch went to checkStateCellsConsistency and NEVER to checkElementCellRender, so the identity/kind/style question was never asked of it. ART001 "Levin's Velolampe" (bible: "A compact rectangular bicycle lamp approximately as long as a child's palm, black matte plastic casing with a flat rear face and a slightly convex circular lens at the front centre, a U-shaped black plastic bracket mounted perpendicular to the underside for clipping to a handlebar, overall length about ten centimetres") rendered in both state cells as a large black broadcast/CCTV-style camera body; the stored cell image was viewed directly. Stored cellGates held a single {gate:'state_cells', ok:true} record reading verbatim "State cells pass: The object is consistent in shape, color, and material, with the only difference being the state of the lamp being off or lit." All five pages holding that reference reproduced the camera. ANI002 and ART002 in the same story had the same blind spot.
bugs.fix: New checkStateBatch asks BOTH questions: identity once against the FIRST (unaltered) cell with the parent's base description, plus the existing cross-state consistency check. The batch fails if either answers NO; the failing reason (prefixed 'object identity:' / 'state consistency:') feeds the single re-render through buildReferenceSheetPrompt's gateReason. Each verdict is recorded separately via recordElementCellGate - identity under gate 'element_cell', consistency under 'state_cells' - so consistency-pass + identity-fail is never stored as a pass. Fail-open at the *_still_bad sites and the one-question/one-re-render shape are unchanged. Cost: +1 judge call per state batch, +2 when a re-render happens. Tests: tests/unit/vb-state-batch-gate.test.ts. See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-11 'A Visual Bible entry with states[] is asked the identity question too'.

bugs.title: A Visual Bible object description built as a geometric parts list renders as whatever everyday object that geometry describes - a bicycle lamp as a CCTV camera, a dragon scale as a seashell
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi, reproduced on fresh renders against current code in Test Lab experiments 1189 and 1190. ART001 "Levin's Velolampe" (bicycle front lamp) rendered as a black CCTV / broadcast camera on 5 of 5 shipped page appearances AND on the Lab re-render, where the identity gate passed it verbatim: "The watercolor painting depicts a black bicycle front lamp with a U-shaped bracket, matching the description and art style". ART002 "Kleine Schuppe" (small dragon scale) rendered as a ceramic dish on the shipped pages and as a scallop shell on the re-render, which the identity gate DID catch: "The object is a seashell, not a dragon scale fragment". Stored descriptions verbatim - lamp: "A compact rectangular bicycle lamp approximately as long as a child's palm, black matte plastic casing with a flat rear face and a slightly convex circular lens at the front centre, a U-shaped black plastic bracket mounted perpendicular to the underside for clipping to a handlebar, overall length about ten centimetres." scale: "A single curved scale fragment roughly the size of a large coin, deep teal-green with a smooth convex outer face and a concave rough inner face, the edges thin and slightly translucent amber, the surface marked with a fine radiating pattern of shallow ridges spreading from the base like a fan." Both name the object correctly and describe it accurately; each is a geometric parts list whose nearest real-world match is a different object. Root cause in our own prompt: the artifact `description` field in prompts/scene-expansion-all.txt instructed "described by shape and parts, never by a style name", with no recognisability requirement - the opposite of the clothing rule that already solves this ("The costume must read as that costume at a glance", story-bible-from-beats.txt).
bugs.fix: prompts/scene-expansion-all.txt: new FIRST bullet of the `description` contract - "It must read as that thing at a glance. Name the thing with the word that names it, and name the one feature that separates it from the everyday object its bare geometry would otherwise describe - what it attaches to, what it is part of, what it does. Geometry serves recognition; it is never the whole description." - and the artifact schema `description` field now opens with the same requirement before size/colour/material/geometry. The "never by a style name" constraint is kept and made subordinate rather than competing. prompts/reference-sheet.txt gains the render-side counterpart as a global REQUIREMENTS line: "Each cell reads as the element it is named as. When the shapes and parts described also fit a commoner everyday object, the cell shows the named one". Deliberately NOT changed: no proportions/stated-dimensions rule (owner rejected that diagnosis - the failure is the wrong object, not wrong sizing), the cell gate's fail-open "accepted anyway" behaviour, and server/lib/referenceSheets.js gate logic. Tests: tests/unit/vb-authoring-contract.test.ts, tests/unit/reference-sheet-mismatch.test.ts. See docs/decisions.md 2026-09-11 'Visual Bible descriptions must read as the named object, not as a parts list'.

bugs.title: A reference cell drew the thing the description named as what the object attaches to - the cell showed the object plus its mounting instead of the object alone
bugs.source: Staging story job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi, Lab experiments 1191 and 1192. Naming what the object attaches to fixed the identity failure (the entry stopped rendering as an unrelated everyday object), but the rendered cells also DREW the mounting. bugs.source: Staging job_1789506283204_3kxqshifx, Levin, pages 8/9/11/13/15/17/18. Reproduced by replaying the real stored inputs (stories.data.clothingRequirements.Levin.standard.description plus the page's own brief METADATA) through extractSceneMetadata -> resolveWornItemsForPage -> resolveOutfitForPage. The contract opens "a solid red, visibly hand-knitted wool cap with a small rolled-up brim around the bottom edge, shaped slightly oversized and wide; ..." - ONE hat, colour in front, fit behind, commas inside the clause and semicolons between clauses. splitClauses (server/lib/wornItems.js) split on /[;,]/ alike, making three clauses of it; only the middle one carried a headwear noun, so ART004 "hand-knitted wool cap" declared off removed that one and left "A solid red; shaped slightly oversized and wide; a forest-green zip-up fleece jacket with a front zip and two patch pockets at the hips; roomy enough to hold an egg pressed against the chest; ..." - the colour, the fit and the jacket's own capacity phrase all now read as garments, and the jacket's internal comma had become a semicolon. NOT confined to a log line: the corrupted string is what wornItems.resolveGeneratedOutfit hands the eval side, and 9 stored strings in job_1789506283204_3kxqshifx are entity-grid judge findings quoting it back - data.finalChecksReport.entity.characters.Levin.issues[2].description reads "The expected red hat, described as 'A solid red; shaped slightly oversized and wide', is missing in cells B (page 13) and D (page 17)", a MAJOR clothing_inconsistent finding demanding the hat be added to the two pages the brief had taken it off, alongside two further MAJOR findings that contradict it and each other.
bugs.fixedIn: b1d117e2b8cfc862926f8ab59fa07101a677ea96 - fix(worn): a clause is never cut at a comma inside it, and a swap needs proof of disagreement
bugs.fix: The delimiters are ranked, structurally, not statistically. A SEMICOLON is always a top-level boundary - over 833 stored staging+prod outfit contracts it never appears inside a garment description. A COMMA is a boundary only between two texts that EACH name a garment through the same closed SLOT_NOUNS vocabulary every other decision in the module uses; a fragment naming no garment is not a clause but a colour, a fit or a trim, and it is merged back into the clause beside it (the one before, or - when it opens the contract - the one after). splitClauses now scans for candidate boundaries at parenthesis depth 0 and returns clause text verbatim from the source, separators and all, so a caller that drops one clause and rejoins the rest changes nothing else. The bias is deliberate: over-splitting DELETES a garment, while under-splitting only makes removeWornItemFromOutfit refuse the strip (slot-clause-carries-another-garment) with the explicit "is NOT wearing" prompt line still carrying the instruction. Proof: the replay was run over every stored page of every story on staging AND prod that carries a visualBible, clothingRequirements and sceneImages - 236 stories, 3,203 (page, character) pairs. 33 pairs were rewritten by the resolver before, 21 after; exactly 22 pairs change, all of them in the two stories above, and ZERO pairs the resolver had previously left alone are touched. Pinned by tests/unit/worn-outfit-clause-corruption.test.ts, whose fixtures are the stored strings and whose last block re-pins the four other stored contracts the resolver rewrites anywhere in staging or prod as byte-identical.

bugs.title: buildRenameMap protected only names held by AGREEING matches, so a rename onto a name an unpaired or box-less match held wrote one name onto two matches and erased a character from matches[]
bugs.source: Reproduced by replaying the real reconcileIdentity over every stored version carrying both an evaluator matches[] and a detector bboxDetection.figures[] - 1,194 versions / 59 stories on staging, 317 / 13 on production - with evaluatorReference/evaluatorCharacter restored so the replay receives exactly what production received. 76 staging versions (20 prod) carry an identity conflict; the agreed-only guard shipped on 2026-09-14 still applied 30 renames on staging and 15 on prod, of which 11 and 12 fabricated a duplicate name. checkIdentityAgreement pairs greedily by nearest centre with no mutual exclusion and only pairs an evaluator name the detector used somewhere within maxCentreDistance; everything else lands in `unpaired` (a name the detector never assigned, a figure whose nearest counterpart was too far, an animal the detector does not name), and a match with no bbox is filtered out before pairing and is in neither list. bugs.title: A wornAs slot the writer invented returned unknown-slot before anything else was tried, so nine pages that took a garment off stripped nothing and every judge kept demanding it
bugs.source: Staging job_1789681157795_wkt20ckod, Levin, pages 9/10/12/13/14/15/16/17/18 - 14 stored (page, item) pairs. Reproduced by replaying the real stored inputs (stories.data.clothingRequirements.Levin.standard.description plus each page's own brief METADATA and the story's Visual Bible) through extractSceneMetadata -> resolveWornItemsForPage -> resolveOutfitForPage, and through the eval-side recompute resolveGeneratedOutfit. The writer linked ART002 "red knitted mittens" (type "handwear") as wornAs: "Levin.hands" and ART003 "rust-orange wool scarf" (type "neckwear") as wornAs: "Levin.neck". Neither "hands" nor "neck" is in WORN_SLOTS - both garments are `accessories`, which is the one slot the two authoring prompts never listed - so removeWornItemFromOutfit hit `SLOT_NOUNS[key] === undefined` and returned {removed: false, reason: "unknown-slot"} on every one of the 14 pairs, before the clause split, before the element-identity route, before anything. parseWornAs accepted "Levin.hands" without a word, so the fault was invisible from the moment it was authored: nothing logged, nothing counted, no finding. The consequence is not a log line - the unstripped string is what promptBuilders sends the image model, what evalPipeline.buildEvalClothingContract hands the quality, semantic and prompt-compliance judges, what the entity grid compares against, and what all three character-repair entry points dress the character in. On pages 14-18 the brief has the scarf wrapped around an egg, spread on the earth, or out of frame, while that one string still says "a long rust-orange wool scarf wound twice around the neck with both ends hanging down the front". Corpus survey over both environments: 15 stored wornAs values in total, 13 naming a real slot (headwear 5, outer layer 4, belt/waist 3, top 1) and 2 outside WORN_SLOTS - both in this one story. `accessories` has never once been used, which is the measurement that identifies the authoring prompt as the source: on the only two occasions a character wore an accessory, the writer invented a slot for it.
bugs.fix: Two halves, both owner-approved. THE RESOLVER: the unknown slot no longer pre-empts the element-identity route added in 4984be189. That route asks the declared Visual Bible element which clause of the contract is itself, from the element's own name / label / aliases / description, and it never needed a slot at all; `SLOT_NOUNS[key]` missing is now only the loss of the FALLBACK vocabulary, not an exit. `unknown-slot` is still the reason reported when identity declines, so the fault never becomes invisible, and clauseRemainderWithoutItem treats an absent vocabulary as an empty one - a refusal, never a crash and never a guess. bugs.title: Every image version reported the FIRST render's prompt as its own, because the version builder fell back to the page-level field
bugs.source: Staging job_1789759147125_p08djwhbl, coverImages.initialPage. Three versions, three different renders, one shared prompt string: v0 source=original (compressedScene 4,227 ch, sha c30302473a), v1 source=iterate-round-1 (compressedScene 1,370 ch, sha 1b39d40f21), v2 source=style-repair-grok (compressedScene 1,370 ch, sha 1b39d40f21) — and all three .prompt identical at 7,366 ch, sha e40958bb51. That string contains v0's compressedScene and neither v1's nor v2's, so it is demonstrably v0's prompt on all three records. `compressedScene` was already resolved per version (resolveVersionCompressedScene) and was correct; `prompt` was not. The consequence is not a missing field but a WRONG one: a reader of imageVersions[1].prompt gets a confident wrong answer, which cost the owner three investigation rounds.
bugs.rootCause: buildVersionEntry (server/lib/repairPipeline.js) stored `prompt: v.prompt || img.prompt || null`, and the round-0 `source:'original'` baseVersion never set `prompt` at all — so the page-level string was substituted into every version that had not recorded one. Four render paths had recorded none: (a) the style-repair version hardcoded `prompt: null` because repairPageStyle never returned the repaint prompt it sent; (b) the iterate round result read only `result.imagePrompt`, which iteratePage returns but iterateCover and the plain-regen branch of executeIterateAction do not — so EVERY cover iterate stored null; (c) char-fix had repairResult.promptSent but routed it only into charFixDetails; (d) inpaint's full sent string was never returned from inpaintPageRegion at all. Two related defects on the cover path: storyJobPipeline's `rawImages.push` for covers omitted `modelId` (the page path carries `modelId: activeModelId`), so every cover entered the repair pipeline model-less and its v0 recorded modelId undefined; and the cover root mirrored `compressedScene` from the shipped version while leaving `prompt` describing the first render, so one cover record narrated two different renders.
bugs.fix: A VERSION'S PROMPT IS ITS OWN OR IT IS NOTHING. buildVersionEntry now calls `resolveOwnRenderPrompt(v)` (server/lib/repairLogic.js) — a named one-argument resolver with NO page parameter, so the `|| img.prompt` that caused this cannot be re-added without changing the call; it also normalises '' and whitespace to null. Every render path stamps its own prompt at creation instead: the v0 original carries `img.prompt` as genuinely its own (it IS the first render), scale-repair carries img.scaleRepairPrompt, each text-space candidate carries its own (the untouched `original` candidate takes the page's), inpaint carries the new `promptSent` (the complete string handed to the editor; `instruction` is only its core), char-fix carries repairResult.promptSent, iterate reads all three branches it dispatches to (`result.promptSent || result.imagePrompt || result.prompt`), and style-repair carries the prompt repairPageStyle now returns. iteratePageCore additionally returns `promptSent` — the POST-shrink string the model really received, not the pre-shrink build — so a version's prompt and its compressedScene describe one render and the containment property that made this diagnosable holds by construction. A path that genuinely sent no prompt (the mechanical garment recolour) stores null; nothing inherits. The page/cover ROOT is a different field with a different job and keeps an original-lineage fallback, expressed through `resolveVersionPrompt(best, img)`: it is a MODEL input on the repair re-run path (repairPipeline interpolates `${img.prompt}` into the string it sends) and the page-level fallback every version consumer now relies on, so a null there would ship the literal "null" to an image model. Both root fields now describe the version that SHIPPED: the cover root's `prompt` is mirrored alongside its `compressedScene`, and the cover push into the repair pipeline stamps `modelId`. Consumers that need the page's prompt read the PAGE record explicitly — buildEvalInputs already did (`entry.prompt || orig.prompt`); the cover-regen "previous" capture was changed from `??` to `||` so a null version prompt no longer short-circuits its cover-root fallback; the client version-switch handler now copies a version prompt onto the page only when it is a non-empty string; ImageVersion.prompt is typed `string | null`. Pinned by tests/unit/version-prompt-is-own-render.test.ts (21 cases).

bugs.title: On a one-pass environment the per-round repair cap DROPS every over-cap page — two pages carrying a CRITICAL shipped with zero repair attempts
bugs.source: staging job_1789759147125_p08djwhbl (18 pages). p14 finalScore 45, imageVersions.length 1, wasRegenerated false, retryHistory = the original generation record only, carrying a clothing CRITICAL; p18 identical at 48 with an action_interaction CRITICAL. Replayed from the stored round-1 evals (scripts/analysis/replay-round1-badpages.js): findBadPages returns 15 bad pages ordered 2, 17, 10, 11, 8, 12, 7, 3, 1, 14, 18, 15, 16, 5, 13, and applyRoundCap admits exactly the first 9 — 2, 17, 10, 11, 8, 12, 7, 3, 1 — which is EXACTLY the set of pages that has a second stored version. p14 and p18 were ranks 10 and 11; p15 and p16 (also CRITICAL-carrying) ranks 12 and 13.
bugs.rootCause: The per-round cap (owner, 2026-09-09) is justified entirely by its deferral contract: "over-cap pages are DEFERRED, not dropped — they are still bad next round and come back". That is only true while a later round exists. runtime.repairMaxPasses is 1 on staging and locally (3 in production), so round 1 IS the last round and every deferral is a silent, permanent drop. Nothing in the loop knew it was the final round, and applyRoundCap had no way to know either — it received only page numbers. The result contradicts the 2026-09-04 ruling that a CRITICAL finding forces a redo regardless of score.
bugs.impact: Every staging/local story with more bad pages than the cap ships its over-cap pages untouched. On this run 6 of 15 bad pages were dropped, 4 of them carrying a CRITICAL (p14, p18, p15, p16). Production (3 passes) is affected only in the milder form: a page still deferred after the last round is dropped the same way.
bugs.fix: applyRoundCap now takes `lastRound` and `criticalPageNums`. When no further round will run, pages carrying a CRITICAL/CATASTROPHIC finding that the cap would otherwise drop are admitted as a RESERVED allowance appended after the score-ranked slice, bounded by LAST_ROUND_CRITICAL_MAX = 5 — the same shape as the book audit allowance, so a many-CRITICAL book cannot become a whole-book regeneration. The cap itself, its shares and both thresholds are unchanged, and a NON-final round still defers exactly as before. repairPipeline passes round >= roundLimit and the round`s critical pages (hasCriticalSeverityFinding over roundEvalPages). The WARN line now says DROPPED rather than DEFERRED on the last round. Replay over the stored run: the 9 previously repaired pages are still admitted in the same order, p14/p18 (and p15/p16) join them, and only p5/p13 — no CRITICAL — stay out. Pinned by tests/unit/repair-gate-cap.test.ts (3 new cases).

bugs.title: A garment seen from behind is described as a different TYPE, and the finding is treated as authoritative — three false findings cost one page 55 points
bugs.source: staging job_1789207854566_l43qgl34w p5 (five figures walking away down a street, every one facing "away from viewer"). Two CRITICAL clothing findings read "black skirt instead of black cropped wide-leg sailor trousers"; a third reads "missing brown buckled boots detail". The shipped image was downloaded and viewed at crop: both figures wear black cropped wide-leg trousers — the split between the legs is visible at the hem — over brown buckled boots. Removing the three findings moves the page from -20 to 35. Stage 1 stored verbatim: figure 3 "red puffed-sleeve coat, black skirt, brown boots", figure 4 "green long-sleeved shirt, black corset, black skirt, brown boots", figure 5 "purple hooded cloak, dark grey or teal trousers, black boots".
bugs.rootCause: Stage 1, the prompt-blind describer (prompts/image-inventory-unified.txt), made the garment-type error; the blind compliance judge reasons entirely over that prose and compared "skirt" to the contract's "trousers" faithfully. `clothing` was the ONLY per-figure field with no abstention vocabulary — eyewear, headwear, facial_hair and worn_carried each carried one — so a describer required to name a type from a back view had to guess at one. Two further faults were the judge's own: it awarded CRITICAL where its own rule already capped this case at MAJOR, and it reported boots missing that stage 1 had reported present ("brown boots", lacking only the word "buckled"). The carve-out naming this exact case existed in the judge and was skipped because it sat two sentences AFTER the sentence awarding CRITICAL, reading as a qualifier on a verdict already reached, and was gated on the judge recognising a garment noun rather than on any machine-readable field.
bugs.impact: Swept 105 staging stories / 1211 pages (626 with a stored inventory), 2026-07-31 to 2026-09-18: 199 of 1464 figures (13.6%) are back-turned, and 59 garment findings sit on a page holding one. 11 of those are CRITICAL and ALL 11 come from the blind compliance judge, which is currently OFF (promptComplianceJudge defaults false, 2026-09-19) — so the CRITICAL path is dormant in production and live in the Lab and behind PROMPT_COMPLIANCE_JUDGE=true. The two evaluators that SEE the image produced 18 such findings and ZERO CRITICAL; one of the 18 is a true instance of the class (a semantic MAJOR calling knee-length breeches "a dark skirt-like garment"). Stage 1 itself is never gated and runs on every page.
bugs.fix: The describer may now abstain: image-inventory-unified.txt's `clothing` field gains `type not visible from this angle` for a lower-body garment seen from behind or at a steep angle (which hides the split between the legs) and an over-garment seen from behind (which hides the front fastening) — the same shape as its existing `cannot tell at this size`, not a parallel mechanism. image-evaluation.txt carries the identical schema sentence (inventory-schema sibling). The blind judge's Clothing type bullet now checks the figure's `facing` BEFORE any severity — the 2026-08-10 hoist shape — and reports no garment-type difference where `facing` is "away from viewer", "left" or "right", nor on an abstention; colour still rules, and an attribute of a named garment the inventory did not itemise is undescribed, never missing. Both sighted judges carry the same rule (N-17 in image-evaluation.txt, a never-flag bullet in image-semantic.txt). No code-side severity change: classification belongs to the prompt. Replayed against the real stored inventory for l43qgl34w p5 — all 5 figures gate, and the three CRITICALs were raised against figures 3, 4 and 5. Pinned by tests/unit/eval-garment-type-camera-angle.test.ts (9 cases).

bugs.title: The landmark guard deletes a finding outright — a guarded page stores fewer findings than the judge emitted, with nothing recording that the guard fired
bugs.source: Staging job_1789759147125_p08djwhbl page 1, read back from stories.data. v0: complianceResult.fixable_issues holds 8 entries, scoreBreakdown.threeStage.issues holds 6; the 2 missing are exactly the two landmark_element:true entries — a MODERATE `setting` ('Setting includes buildings, church steeple, tiled roofs...') and a CRITICAL `object_presence` ('Ground surface described as cracked pavement rather than gravel'). v1: 4 and 3, the missing one again the landmark_element:true CRITICAL.

The suppression of the DEDUCTION is correct and intended — an unmasked whole-frame removal would erase the real place the page depicts — but it was implemented as deletion of the RECORD, so no stored field anywhere distinguishes a page the guard fired on from a page the judge found nothing on. The guard's WARN log is the only witness, and logs are not stored data.
bugs.impact: Every protected landmark page. Stored eval data silently disagrees with the judge's own complianceResult, so any later audit of judge precision, guard precision or finding counts reads short — and the guard's own false-drop rate (11 of 15 measured fires on staging were a prop, not the landmark, before the 2026-09-18 subject trigger) cannot be measured from stored rows at all.
