No text matching: the guard still triggers on the declared landmark_element field and the `fix` edit instruction. Pinned by tests/unit/landmark-suppressed-record.test.ts (9 cases, fixtures are the real stored p1 findings), including an explicit score-identity assertion.

bugs.title: A named creature whose ONLY declaration is its own pages[] never reaches the judge's EXPECTED CAST — 68 of 1,392 stored pages
bugs.source: Owner brief cited missing_character findings naming off-roster subjects — the dog "Nia", a dragon, a grey tomcat. Re-measured against the REAL roster builder over 127 staging stories: those named creatures are ALREADY on the roster (the includeAnimals opt-in added to buildSecondaryExpectedCharacters 2026-09-10, and collectSceneObjectFigureNames 2026-09-12); the stored findings naming them are from runs on the older code. The residual hole is narrower and was confirmed by replay: buildSecondaryExpectedForPage reads an entry's own pages[] declaration and read vb.secondaryCharacters ONLY, never vb.animals — so a creature the scene metadata does not list and whose VB id is not filed in objects[] reaches no roster at all. Replay over 1,392 stored pages: 68 pages (4.9%) are missing at least one such creature — "Nia" on eight pages of job_1789147573901_m3uam0nxi, plus "Fauchi", "Nebel", "Grosser Rabe"/"Kleiner Rabe", "Beni".
bugs.rootCause: buildSecondaryExpectedForPage (server/lib/promptBuilders.js) is one of three enrichment paths in buildExpectedCastBlock and the only one that reads a Visual Bible entry's own pages[] declaration. It enumerated vb.secondaryCharacters only, although vb.animals entries carry pages[] in exactly the same shape. Secondarily its description builder read only human fields (hair/face/clothing), so a creature with no prose `description` would still have been dropped by its `if (!desc) continue` guard once the pool was in scope.
bugs.impact: 68 of 1,392 stored staging pages (4.9%), purely additive — no page loses a roster name. On those pages the judge was never told a named creature was staged, so an absent one could not be reported and a drawn one could be read as a surplus figure. NOT FIXED BY THIS, measured the same way: of 85 distinct missing_character subjects in the corpus, 16 are off-roster and ALL 16 name a figure in no Visual Bible pool at all — a separate defect (a judge inventing a name), untriaged.
bugs.fix: buildSecondaryExpectedForPage takes the same `includeAnimals` opt-in its sibling buildSecondaryCharacterDescriptions already has, default OFF, and the evaluator roster opts in — an extension of the existing enrichment, not a second roster builder. It stays off by default because the other caller is the DETECTOR roster (storyJobPipeline), where the owner's 2026-08-19 ruling holds: GroundingDINO detects `person`, so an animal on a detector roster is a guaranteed missing person. Its description builder now also reads species/coloring/features. Nothing identity-matches a creature against a photo it does not have: the photo-backed cast is sceneCharacters alone, vbNonHumanNames already pools vb.animals so the new entries land in nonHumanNames and stay out of the people arithmetic, and charRepairTarget never passes pageNumber so this branch does not run on the repair path. testlab.js calls the same builder with pageNumber, so the Lab mirror inherits the fix. Pinned by tests/unit/creature-declares-page-roster.test.ts (11 cases, real stored Visual Bible).

bugs.title: The arc-hints stage was never told which source wins, so it emitted a hint undoing the first meeting the arc staged — and the planner obeyed it
bugs.source: Staging job_1789853503332_riqncqg1i, read back from stories.data. The commission stages four boys who do not know each other; a main character's saved profile names two of them as his good friends. The arc honoured the commission. arcReviewReport.arcHints then carried "ISSUE: The boys introduce themselves as strangers even though [the main character]'s details already name [two of them] as his good friends -> CHANGE: Have them greet one another by name as friends who spotted the egg together". bugs.rootCause: The 2026-09-19 character-source split (characterSourceRule(), commits 54da822b1 / f1c589a83) injected one constant into four prompts — arc-create.txt, arc-retell.txt, story-arc-review.txt (master 'premise') and story-beats.txt (master 'arc'). prompts/arc-hints.txt is a FIFTH stage reading the same two inputs, {CHARACTER_DETAILS} and the story, and was not a member of the set, so it declared no {CHARACTER_SOURCE_RULE} and buildArcHintsPrompt filled none. The template's THE FINAL ARC block moved above CHARACTER DETAILS so the rule's "the arc above" is literal. Second guard: HINT_VS_ARC_RULE, one new constant, is appended to BOTH arc-hint headings (the declared sibling pair arc-hint-handoff) extending the existing picture-rule guard rather than competing with it. sibling-registry.json's character-source-claim set gains arc-hints.txt as a fifth member. bugs.title: The trial story-complete mail minted its claim token with an unrequired `crypto`, so the link AND the PDF were silently dropped — and every mail greeted the user by their email address
bugs.source: Owner-confirmed, verified against production users. storyJobPipeline.js called crypto.randomBytes(32) with no require("crypto") in that file; Node's global crypto is WebCrypto and has no randomBytes (reproduced: TypeError: globalThis.crypto.randomBytes is not a function). The throw landed in the catch that labels it "Failed to generate trial PDF for email", so the failure was logged as a PDF problem and the email went out with neither claim link nor attachment. Greeting: 68 of 69 prod users with a real email have no shipping_first_name and a username that IS their email address, so greeting resolved to the address in all 7 templates x 4 languages.
bugs.rootCause: Commit 7ac04a42b (2026-08-11) extracted the pipeline out of server.js and left `const crypto = require("crypto")` behind at server.js:18. Separately, the claim link was gated on trial ORIGIN (is_trial || trial_data IS NOT NULL) rather than claim STATE, and the greeting name was a hand-copied `shipping_first_name || username.split(" ")[0]` expression duplicated at four sites.
bugs.impact: LIVE ON PRODUCTION since 2026-08-11. Every trial story-complete email: no claim link, no PDF. Fixing crypto alone would have started mailing "claim your account" links to the 14 of 17 trial-origin prod accounts that are already converted. Greeting defect affects story-complete, trial-story-complete, trial-reminder, story-failed, order-confirmation, order-shipped and order-failed in all four languages.
bugs.fix: storyJobPipeline.js requires node crypto. Both claim-minting sites (storyJobPipeline.js unified completion mail, server/lib/trialEmail.js) gate the claim link on claim STATE — is_trial === true && has_set_password !== true — matching the gate trialReminders.js already used; the PDF stays gated on trial origin by design. Greeting resolution collapsed into one exported helper, email.resolveGreetingName(), which rejects any candidate containing "@"; the 56 template salutations became "Hallo{greeting}," so a nameless greeting renders bare, and order-failed's four gendered salutations (Dear / Liebe/r / Cher-Chère / Caro-Cara) became the neutral forms the other templates use. Pinned by tests/unit/email-greeting-and-claim-gate.test.ts.

bugs.source: Reproduced from stored data, dragon run 6 (staging job_1790100385959_1nitlympp) p17: v0 prompt names none of Levin/Julian/Max/Kiaan; the iterate repair v1 prompt names each 3 times and carries a HEIGHT ORDER block; the page stores unrepairedCritical missing_character "Levin is absent … EXPECTED CAST of 4". v1 (45) beat v0 (43) and shipped: the hatchling is drawn as a red copy of the adult dragon and the eggshell is gone.

bugs.fix: Owner-approved severity rule (code, structural): runEntityConsistencyChecks stamps each character's declaredOffByPage (from the same per-appearance offIds that key the grids, i.e. the page's wornItems rows); scoring.offByDesignFinding voids a finding on a page when it bills as clothing (evalBuckets), the page declares >=1 of the character's garments off, and the finding's clothingCategory is not that exact off-state grid (or is unknown). entityIssuesForPage returns it under excused (0 points), never in issues, so it never reaches the consolidator, the panel list or char-fix; entityConsistency logs each one. Stamps now carry clothingCategory and Step 4b dedupes per grid. No prompt change: the judge already gets the page state through the --off: grid (17bbd887a). Replay: p11 v0 70->85, p12 v1 -15->0, p16 v0 13->28; p9 (Max ART005 off) unchanged 75.

bugs.title: The global generation tracker silently dropped any job still processing after 60 minutes, while production stories run 52-83 minutes
bugs.source: Coordinator-confirmed 2026-09-24 from code plus measured production durations (52, 54, 57, 58, 83 min). client/src/context/GenerationContext.tsx cleared the active job when Date.now()-startedAt > 60 min while the server still reported processing.
bugs.rootCause: A client-side ORPHANED_JOB_THRESHOLD_MS (60 min) age cutoff, set when stories took minutes, second-guessed the server; the server status route already marks a stalled job failed (10-minute heartbeat watchdog, 180-minute backstop).
bugs.impact: Readers who left the wizard (as the wait screen now tells them to) lost the nav %, the My Stories generating card and the auto-open on completion after minute 60 of every long story; only the email remained.
bugs.fix: Removed the 60-minute orphan cutoff and the 24h restore cap. The tracker ends only on a terminal server status via jobStatusOutcome (client/src/context/jobStatusOutcome.ts): completed, failed/cancelled (silent for stalls, abandonment and user cancels), or the row gone (404). Pinned in tests/unit/generation-tracking-no-age-cutoff.test.ts.

bugs.title: describeFigureForRepair embedded the whole outfit sentence, so cast and creature names and a garment the page takes off reached the image model

bugs.title: A repair that repaints pixels was never told the page's declared light: the p15 inpaint turned a declared foggy night into golden daylight, and the repaired version shipped at 100
bugs.source: Owner-reported, staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7 p15 (brief timeOfDay night, weather fog). Stored imageVersions[1].prompt is exactly "Fix these issues in this children's book illustration:\n1. Remove the visible street lamp from the background." with no light; v1 pixels are warm daylight; v1 finalScore 100 (semantic visible.setting "A forest at night").
bugs.rootCause: The LIGHT line (sceneLight.buildLightLine) reached only the page and plate prompts. inpaintPage, the character repair (faceRepair.buildPrompt), the scale repair and the manual /repair/image route built their prompts without it. The pipeline re-eval did carry DECLARED LIGHT night, fog (replayed from the stored inputs) and the judge missed the daylight on that run; the manual /repair/image and /repair-workflow/character-repair re-evals ran quality-only, so no judge saw the light there.
bugs.impact: A repair can silently change a page's time of day and weather and still win pick-best.
bugs.fix: sceneLight.buildRepairLightLine closes every repaint prompt (images.buildInpaintInstruction, used by the pipeline, the Lab and the manual route; faceRepair.buildPrompt, every branch; scaleRepair.buildScaleRepairPrompt). The two manual routes pass page text + brief, so the semantic judge runs and judges light as on a first render. Replay of the stored p15 instruction now ends on the night/fog LIGHT line; Lab #1471 re-judged stored v1 against DECLARED LIGHT night, fog and flagged it as daytime (MODERATE).

bugs.title: A landmark plate prompt over the Grok cap (once the magenta prefix was added) was refused by the local shrink, caught as a Grok failure, and painted by Gemini as a photograph
bugs.source: Stored evidence, staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7: the p1 and p11 landmark plate prompts are 7,552 and 7,463 chars; the plates came back from gemini-2.5-flash-image photographic, with signatures and paper mats, and the covers were refused (IMAGE_OTHER). Replay of shrinkPromptForModel(prompt, 7900 - 612) on both: throws "refusing to cut them".
bugs.rootCause: editWithGrok prepends the 612-char magenta-extension prefix and refits the body via fitGrokPromptWithPrefix -> sectionAwareCut. A plate prompt opens with **ART STYLE:**, a must-keep marker of the PAGE prompt, so the whole plate read as protected tail and the cut threw. The dispatcher's Grok catch treated that local throw as a Grok failure and fell back to Gemini. Vantage plate prompts also carried the Art Director prose twice (v.description equals the vantage plate, emitted again as FRAMING).
bugs.impact: Landmark plates on Gemini (photographic, lettering, paper mats) and lost covers, with the real cause hidden behind a provider fallback.
bugs.fix: AD prose emitted once; plate calls fitted by fitPlatePrompt (own cut order: landmark photo note, over-the-shoulder line; nothing else cut) against cap minus the worst-case magenta prefix (616); PromptFitError is rethrown by every provider-fallback catch (rethrowLocalFault, prompt_fit_failed error event) instead of falling back. Replay over 134 stored plate prompts (both DBs, 14 days): 134/134 fit, none cut, largest landmark plate 7,267 + 616 = 7,883.

bugs.title: An angled page whose vantage base plate was already painted in its camera got a second, needless camera derive
bugs.source: Stored evidence, staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7: p10 (LOC002.1, ultra-wide, alone on its vantage) and p14 (LOC001.4, high-angle, alone) carry plateDerivedFor ultra-wide / high-angle although their base plates were painted from those same pages' shots.
bugs.rootCause: The derive loop (storyJobPipeline.js vantage plates) compared the page's plate class with PLATE_BASE_CLASS ('eye-level') only, not with the class the base was actually painted in; a vantage with no eye-level page paints its base from its angled page.
bugs.impact: An extra paid Grok edit per such page that can only drift the place away from its base; the derive instruction also claimed the base was painted at eye level.
bugs.fix: plateEditForPage (server/lib/platePlan.js) derives a camera move only when the page class differs from plateClass(vantageShot), a re-light only when the light differs; the derive names the base's real shot. Replay on the stored run: old logic reproduces all 18 stored plateDerivedFor values; new logic 4 derives instead of 6, p10 and p14 share their base.

bugs.title: Every in-generation iterate repair on a story page failed with "No scene description found for page N"
bugs.source: Stored evidence, staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7: finalChecksReport.repairRounds holds the p7 and p14 iterate rounds with error "No scene description found for page N" and no image, while stories.data.sceneDescriptions carries both briefs under `description`. Replay of the iterate scene lookup over the stored briefs in the generation shape: throws for p7 and p14.
bugs.rootCause: storyJobPipeline.js handed the repair pipeline `sceneDescriptions: expandedScenes`, whose brief field is `sceneDescription`; iteratePageCore (like every reader of storyData.sceneDescriptions) reads `description`. It used to paper over the mismatch with `description || sceneDescription`; covers-as-pages (6fbd2b599) made a missing `description` a throw, so every in-generation page iterate failed.
bugs.impact: No story page could be repaired by iterate during generation since 2026-09-24; pages shipped at their pre-iterate score. Entity consistency's worn-item and cast lookups read the same field.
bugs.fix: One projection, sceneMetadata.sceneDescriptionRecord, builds the stored sceneDescriptions record (brief under `description`) for the stored story AND for the repair pipeline's story data (projected at repair time, so a side-mirrored brief is the one iterated). iteratePageCore's lookup is resolveIterateScene; the `|| sceneDescription` aliases in images.js and entityConsistency.js are gone. Replay over the stored p7/p14 briefs: old input throws, fixed input resolves the stored brief.

bugs.title: CENTRAL_FIGURE_ABSENT_THIRD filed must-fix findings for all three thirds of a book that stages the central figure on most pages
bugs.source: Stored evidence, staging testlab_experiments #1488 and #1489 (beats_replan on the arc of #1483, job_1790277448294_5herh01j7): results[0].report.castFindings carry "the central figure (das Ei / Marroni) is in frame on no page of the setup/middle/ending" while the plan stages the egg on pages 3-4, 7-11 and 15-16. The stored ROSTER lists "the egg" under things on pages 15-16 only. #1491 carries the same finding.
bugs.rootCause: planCounters.centralFigureAbsentThirds matched the arc STORY LOGIC names whole-word against the plan-check ROSTER. The logic line gave the name in the book language ("das Ei", the arc prompts keep names as they will appear in the book) against an English roster, and the roster reads the who column, which carries people, so an object-like figure staged in the instant never reached it.
bugs.impact: Three false must-fix findings per affected plan, which the re-plan must answer by adding the figure to pages. Lab only: 0 staging and 0 production stories since cf672a0f8.
bugs.fix: The plan check (handed the name in Q12) answers a CENTRAL line with the pages whose picture shows the figure; parsePlanCheckCentralPages reads it and the counter counts on it. The name-vs-roster matcher is deleted; a missing CENTRAL line files nothing and logs an error. Test: the #1488 shape (German name, English roster) returned three thirds before and none now.
